mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate level is inversely related to S&P 500 forward returns: a lower rate (as measured by FEDFUNDS) predicts positive 20-day returns because it reduces the risk-free rate and increases equity valuation multiples.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns show no negative correlation: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window (p-value > 0.05 for negative Rank IC).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 9.5% indicates a deteriorating labor market that signals recessionary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 9.5% and 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances (p-value > 0.05 for negative returns in a one-sample t-test against zero).

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of high unemployment (UNRATE > 9.5%) and low housing starts (HOUST < 600) indicates a severe economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 9.5% AND HOUST < 600 and 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances (p-value > 0.05 for negative returns in a one-sample t-test against zero).

mechanism_narrative: During post-recession recovery periods (as indicated by RSAFS growth rate > 0.5% monthly), the S&P 500 exhibits positive forward returns over the next 20 days due to improving consumer spending.
failure_condition: In the post-recession recovery regime (RSAFS growth rate > 0.5%), SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns in a one-sample t-test against zero).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 90 (INDPRO) indicates a contraction in the real economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 90 and 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances (p-value > 0.05 for negative returns in a one-sample t-test against zero).

mechanism_narrative: The consumer price index level (CPIAUCSL) is inversely related to S&P 500 forward returns: a lower CPI (within the typical range) predicts positive returns over the next 60 trading days because stable inflation supports equity valuations.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL and 60-day returns show no negative correlation: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window (p-value > 0.05 for negative Rank IC).

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS <= 0.5%) and low consumer price index (CPIAUCSL <= 218.5) indicates a stable monetary environment that supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS <= 0.5% AND CPIAUCSL <= 218.5 and 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns in a one-sample t-test against zero).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts below 600 (HOUST) indicates weak consumer demand and predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST < 600 and 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances (p-value > 0.05 for negative returns in a one-sample t-test against zero).
